epoch_ai.synthesis: Oct 2: Epoch estimates the high-bandwidth memory projected to ship 2025-2027 is enough for GPUs running agents equal in weekly working hours to 140-700 million full-time workers on top-tier models, or about 1.9 billion concurrent agents on a cheaper model (DeepSeek V4 Pro). For scale it cites about 100 million US knowledge workers, and it calls demand, not supply, the open question. Read via direct fetch (the cron's Epoch pull is 403-blocked).

semianalysis.synthesis: Oct 5: SemiAnalysis's own Tokenomics model puts consumer subscriptions at 10% of Anthropic's revenue but over 40% of its inference compute. The headline 5x-value comparison with OpenAI's plans rests on figures not in the readable text (the post is paywalled partway), and the model's method is undisclosed.

farmdoc_daily.synthesis: Oct 5: August CPI food prices were 2.7% above a year earlier (at home 2.2%, away from home 3.4%), beef and veal 5.9%; since December 2019, food at home is up 33.0% and away from home 38.1%. USDA forecasts beef and veal up 9.4% for 2026, on 28.5 million beef cows (July 1, down 1%), and the author expects herd rebuilding to take two to three years.

drought_monitor.synthesis: Indiana as of Sept 29: 10.0% abnormally dry (D0), 0.0% moderate drought (D1). Weekly D0 since Sept 1 has run 0.1%, 3.8%, 8.7%, 3.2%, 10.0%: uneven but up overall, with no drought (D1) in any week.

nass_crop_progress.synthesis: Week ending Oct 4, Indiana corn: 99% dented, 77% mature (62% a week earlier), 21% harvested for grain (13%); soybeans 86% dropping leaves (74%), 27% harvested (14%).

interconnection_fyi.synthesis: Indiana holds 56 tracked data-center projects (33 proposed, 13 cancelled, 6 under construction, 4 operational), unchanged in all 23 snapshots since Sept 12. Lake (9) and Porter (7) counties lead.

noaa_ncei_monthly.synthesis: August 2026, Indiana, revised as more station reports came in (678 station-months, from 650): 7.1 in. precipitation and 73.3°F average, against 7.2 in. and 73.0°F last week; Michigan 67.9°F, 2.9 in. September has not posted yet.

equitable_growth.synthesis: Oct 1: from Oct 1, 2026 states pay 75% of SNAP's administrative costs, up from 50%; the same law stops the federal government paying all benefits in states whose payment error rate, averaged over three years, exceeds 6%. About 42 million people, one American in eight, receive SNAP; the piece gives no Indiana or Michigan figures.

ipcc.synthesis: Sept 28: nearly 200 authors are in Bangkok (Sept 8 to Oct 1) for the Working Group III second lead-author meeting on AR7 mitigation; a First-Order Draft, open to expert review, follows. Otherwise administrative items.

beige_book.synthesis: Sept 2 Beige Book, Chicago District: activity rose slightly in July and early August; consumer spending and construction and real estate were flat on balance, business spending fell slightly, prices rose moderately, and farm income expectations for 2026 improved some. Nationally, growth was modest: 10 of 12 Districts reported slight to moderate growth and two reported no change. Next edition Oct 14.

indiana_dnr_water.synthesis: Indiana DNR, August: statewide rainfall 200% of normal and all 12 tracked streams above normal. Groundwater: above normal at 4 of 9 wells, near normal at 4, well below normal at 1 (LaGrange 2). Drought Monitor showed isolated abnormally-dry spots (Sept 8), and the seasonal outlook has no drought through at least November.

fia_indiana.synthesis: USFS 2025 evaluation for Indiana: 4.83M acres of forest, 14.07B cu ft growing stock. Annual mortality is 1.18% of standing volume (sampling error 5.5%), essentially level with 1.19% in the 2024 evaluation; net growth is 2.23%. First reading in this series.

mrcc_monthly_summary.synthesis: Midwest average temperature for August 2026 was 71.8°F, 0.9°F above the 1991-2020 normal (MRCC monthly summary). First reading in this series; the September summary is not out yet.

interconnection_fyi_national.synthesis: Unchanged from the first reading on Sept 29: across 46 US state pages, the largest active pipelines are Virginia (329), Texas (282) and Ohio (86); Indiana is 4th at 39 (4.0% of 972) but 32nd in operating sites (4 of 2,435). The tracker's headline count still does not reconcile with its state pages, so read ranks as rough.

epoch_datacenters.synthesis: Epoch's covered set of 93 large AI data centers rose from 13.5 GW to 13.8 GW over the week, mostly Malaysia (0.56 to 0.89 GW); the US share fell from 88% to 86% at about 11.85 GW. Indiana is unchanged at 1.09 GW across three sites (New Carlisle 910 MW), now 7.9% of the covered total against 8.1%. Dataset updated Oct 5.
